title: Rollout breathe-cycle notebook (personal draft)
content:
Context: quick personal scratchpad for a small-traffic rollout pattern I want to try on staging -> prod. NOT an official runbook yet — packing up heuristics from recent experiments. Keep light; aim is repeatable micro-actions teams can do without heavy ops.

High-level idea (metaphor: breathe-cycle)
- Inhale: small, intentional traffic allocation to the new variant to gather warmup signals and first-order correctness.
- Pause (hold): keep traffic stable while client-side and server-side caches (prefix, KV) accumulate; collect quality and perf metrics.
- Exhale: release remaining traffic if metrics are green, otherwise retract and iterate.

Why this? Observed that immediate ramping often spikes p95 and causes cold-cache hallucination regressions. A short hold at low fraction gives better final stability and fewer rollbacks.

Quick sequence (staging -> prod pattern)
1) Staging smoke (manual) — 0% prod. Run sanity tests, safety evals, smoke scripts (15–30m). Ensure no obvious token-level regressions.
2) Prod micro-canary (inhale) — 0.5% of traffic or a single low-volume tenant cohort. Duration: 20–30m. Purpose: functional + cache priming.
3) Hold window — keep at 0.5% for 45–90m. Watch rolling windows for trends. Do not touch routing unless a critical alert surfaces.
4) Secondary probe — increase to 2% for 30m if hold metrics stable.
5) Medium ramp — 10% for 60m, then 25% for 30m if stable.
6) Final commit — move to target (50–100%) with a staged sequence depending on capacity.

Notes on cohort selection
- Prefer tenants with tolerant SLAs (internal, staging-mimic clients). Avoid high-value enterprise customers until 25%+.
- If feature flags exist, route low-risk flows first (e.g., single-turn completions vs. long chat state flows).
- Use cookie-based affinity for cohorts to avoid churn in cache state.

Warmup tactics (server + client)
- Pre-warm KV caches by issuing low-cost priming requests from a warmup harness (token-limited prompts that access common prefixes).
- Nudge clients to send short prefix requests during inhale window to build useful cache entries.
- If quantized model variant has larger cold-start cost, increase inhale duration.

What to watch (observables)
- Latency: p50/p90/p95, and moving-window delta vs baseline (5m/30m)
- Error rate: 5xx, client retries, ASR-like failures (if applicable)
- Quality regressions: automated eval against small prompt set (pass/fail), ratio of fallback triggers
- Cost signals: per-token compute time, GPU utilization by server variant
- Drift flags: repeat prompt divergence (measuring consistency tier)
- Telemetry anomalies: request size distribution, KV hit rate

Hard abort conditions (immediate rollback)
- p95 > baseline + 150ms sustained for >10m AND error rate > 0.5% absolute
- Any catastrophic error spike (>1% 5xx) or safety violation trigger
- Automated quality eval drop > 5% relative to baseline on the golden prompt set

Soft abort / pause conditions (hold or backoff)
- Gradual p95 uptick (baseline + 70–150ms) OR small error uptick but within teams’ tolerance: pause ramp, extend hold window, run deeper diagnostics
- KV hit rate not increasing as expected after 30m of inhale: investigate cache key patterns

Pinning considerations
- Don't flip global model pin immediately. Use route-level pinning for the cohort to limit blast radius.
- Record exact model digest/hash and serving config in the release note and attach to rollout ticket.
- If using dedicated pools, ensure autoscale headroom is reserved in the next hour to avoid forced fallbacks.

Rollback hygiene
- Pre-create a rollback PR or CLI script that pins the route back to previous digest and rebalances traffic. Test it once in staging.
- Communicate rollback channel and post-rollout reconciliation owner in the ticket.

Communication cadence
- Kickoff message in #release-watch with initial health expectations and who’s oncall.
- Progress pings: inhale start, hold milestone (30m), secondary probe start, medium ramp start, final commit.
- Postmortem stub created automatically on rollback.

Open questions / TODO
- (Q) Ideal inhale fraction vs tenant size — threshold table required. TODO: simulate with synthetic traffic and update guidance.
- (Q) Should we pre-warm with real client traffic via a standby tenant or use synthetic harness? Experiment: 2x runs next week.
- Add short checklist snippet to repo tooling so engineers can run the inhale/hold/exhale sequence from CLI.
- Tie golden prompt automated eval to rollout gates (small lightweight run during hold window).

Quick checklist (for my own use)
- [ ] create ticket + tag owners
- [ ] paste model digest + config into ticket
- [ ] run staging smoke harness (links in ticket)
- [ ] allocate cohort and set affinity cookie
- [ ] start inhale (0.5%), announce in channel
- [ ] monitor core metrics for 45–90m
- [ ] run golden prompt eval (pass threshold set)
- [ ] decide probe -> ramp or rollback
- [ ] document final state and close ticket

Hand-off notes for whoever runs this next
- If you're nervous about p95, favor longer holds at 0.5% and more frequent evaluation rather than faster ramps.
- If dedicated pool saturates, abort and fall back to hosted variant; do not exceed predefined GPU headroom.
- Keep a short log in the ticket with timestamps for all traffic changes (helps later analysis).

Rough scribbles / heuristics (informal)
- inhale = priming, hold = signal smoothing, exhale = commit
- tiny cohorts give you cache wins without client-facing noise
- some clients will oscillate token lengths; watch token-size histograms if quality moves

References / links for later
- Warmup harness script: //github.com/redwood-inference/warmup-harness (TODO add exact path)
- Golden prompts set: confluence://RB-golden-prompts
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1298

End of scratchpad — keep light and iterate. If this proves stable across two more runs, convert into a formal runbook and add CLI helper.
